Introduction:
Hydrodynamic approaches effectively model the intricate dynamics of complex many-body systems, which are often intractable using standard many-body techniques (see, e.g., Refs. 1, 2 for reviews). These methods are particularly useful for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, as illustrated by recent applications in ultracold atomic gases (e.g., 3–10). To address this, general quantum hydrodynamic methods have been proposed (13–15), and recently, a connection was established between these and the positive-P phase-space formulation (16). However, implementing these approaches remains difficult, as they typically require discretizing spatial coordinates, an process that often introduces significant numerical artifacts. To overcome these limitations, we recently introduced a new stochastic hydrodynamic framework directly on the positive-P phase-space, termed the "quantum-Boltzmann" method (17), which has been successfully applied to various quantum many-body problems (18–20).
